defmodule AuthProxy.TokenCache do
  use GenServer

  @moduledoc """
  Caches cross-service authentication tokens with automatic refresh.
  Uses ETS for fast concurrent reads with GenServer managing lifecycle.
  """

  @table :token_cache
  @refresh_interval 270_000
  @token_ttl 300_000

  def start_link(opts) do
    GenServer.start_link(__MODULE__, opts, name: __MODULE__)
  end

  def init(_opts) do
    :ets.new(@table, [:named_table, :public, read_concurrency: true])
    schedule_refresh()
    {:ok, %{pending_callbacks: %{}, request_counter: 0}}
  end

  @doc "Fetch token for a given service, with async refresh if expired"
  def get_token(service_name, callback_pid \\ nil) do
    case :ets.lookup(@table, service_name) do
      [{^service_name, token, expires_at}] ->
        if System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) < expires_at do
          {:ok, token}
        else
          GenServer.call(__MODULE__, {:refresh_token, service_name, callback_pid})
        end
      [] ->
        GenServer.call(__MODULE__, {:refresh_token, service_name, callback_pid})
    end
  end

  @doc "Register an async callback for token refresh notification"
  def register_refresh_callback(service_name, callback_fn) do
    GenServer.cast(__MODULE__, {:register_callback, service_name, callback_fn})
  end

  def handle_call({:refresh_token, service_name, callback_pid}, from, state) do
    request_id = state.request_counter + 1
    
    # Monitor the caller so we can clean up if they die
    {caller_pid, _} = from
    monitor_ref = Process.monitor(caller_pid)

    # Store the caller reference for async response
    updated_pending = Map.put(state.pending_callbacks, request_id, %{
      from: from,
      service: service_name,
      callback_pid: callback_pid,
      monitor_ref: monitor_ref,
      timestamp: System.monotonic_time(:millisecond)
    })

    # Spawn async token fetch
    spawn(fn ->
      token_result = fetch_remote_token(service_name)
      GenServer.cast(__MODULE__, {:token_fetched, request_id, token_result})
    end)

    {:noreply, %{state | pending_callbacks: updated_pending, request_counter: request_id}}
  end

  def handle_cast({:token_fetched, request_id, result}, state) do
    case Map.pop(state.pending_callbacks, request_id) do
      {nil, _} ->
        {:noreply, state}
      {pending_info, remaining_callbacks} ->
        # Demonitor since we're done with this request
        Process.demonitor(pending_info.monitor_ref, [:flush])
        
        case result do
          {:ok, token, ttl} ->
            expires_at = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) + ttl
            :ets.insert(@table, {pending_info.service, token, expires_at})
            GenServer.reply(pending_info.from, {:ok, token})
            
            # Execute registered callbacks with the new token - validate target is alive
            notify_callbacks(pending_info.service, token, pending_info.callback_pid)

          {:error, reason} ->
            GenServer.reply(pending_info.from, {:error, reason})
        end
        {:noreply, %{state | pending_callbacks: remaining_callbacks}}
    end
  end

  def handle_cast({:register_callback, service_name, callback_fn}, state) do
    # Store callback function reference in ETS for cross-process access
    existing = case :ets.lookup(@table, {:callbacks, service_name}) do
      [{{:callbacks, ^service_name}, callbacks}] -> callbacks
      [] -> []
    end
    :ets.insert(@table, {{:callbacks, service_name}, [callback_fn | existing]})
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  def handle_info(:scheduled_refresh, state) do
    # Refresh all cached tokens proactively
    :ets.foldl(fn
      {service_name, _token, _expires} when is_binary(service_name) ->
        spawn(fn ->
          case fetch_remote_token(service_name) do
            {:ok, token, ttl} ->
              expires_at = System.monotonic_time(:millisecond) + ttl
              :ets.insert(@table, {service_name, token, expires_at})
              notify_callbacks(service_name, token, nil)
            _ -> :ok
          end
        end)
      _ -> :ok
    end, :ok, @table)
    
    schedule_refresh()
    {:noreply, state}
  end

  def handle_info({:DOWN, ref, :process, _pid, _reason}, state) do
    # Clean up pending callbacks for dead callers
    cleaned = state.pending_callbacks
    |> Enum.reject(fn {_id, info} -> info.monitor_ref == ref end)
    |> Map.new()
    
    {:noreply, %{state | pending_callbacks: cleaned}}
  end

  defp notify_callbacks(service_name, token, callback_pid) do
    # Only send to callback_pid if it's still alive
    if callback_pid && Process.alive?(callback_pid) do
      send(callback_pid, {:auth_token_refreshed, token})
    end

    # Execute registered callbacks from ETS
    case :ets.lookup(@table, {:callbacks, service_name}) do
      [{{:callbacks, ^service_name}, callbacks}] ->
        Enum.each(callbacks, fn cb ->
          spawn(fn -> cb.(token) end)
        end)
      [] -> :ok
    end
  end

  defp fetch_remote_token(service_name) do
    # Cross-service token fetch with HMAC validation.
    # Require an explicitly configured signing secret; never fall back to a
    # hardcoded/predictable default which would allow signature forgery.
    secret =
      case Application.get_env(:auth_proxy, :signing_secret) do
        nil ->
          raise "AuthProxy signing secret is not configured (:auth_proxy, :signing_secret)"
        "" ->
          raise "AuthProxy signing secret is not configured (:auth_proxy, :signing_secret)"
        value ->
          value
      end

    timestamp = System.system_time(:second)
    payload = "#{service_name}:#{timestamp}"
    signature = :crypto.mac(:hmac, :sha256, secret, payload)
    
    case HTTPClient.post("https://auth.internal/token", %{
      service: service_name,
      timestamp: timestamp,
      signature: Base.encode64(signature)
    }) do
      {:ok, %{status: 200, body: body}} ->
        {:ok, body["token"], body["ttl"] || @token_ttl}
      {:ok, %{status: status}} ->
        {:error, {:http_error, status}}
      {:error, reason} ->
        {:error, reason}
    end
  end

  defp schedule_refresh do
    Process.send_after(self(), :scheduled_refresh, @refresh_interval)
  end
end

defmodule AuthProxy.RequestHandler do
  @moduledoc "Handles incoming requests requiring cross-service auth"

  def handle_request(conn, service_name) do
    # Pass the connection owner PID for safe notification
    callback_pid = conn.owner

    case AuthProxy.TokenCache.get_token(service_name, callback_pid) do
      {:ok, token} ->
        forward_request(conn, token)
      {:error, _reason} ->
        {:error, :auth_failed}
    end
  end

  defp forward_request(conn, token) do
    # Forward with auth token
    {:ok, %{conn | assigns: Map.put(conn.assigns, :auth_token, token)}}
  end
end
